title: Institution identity, lifecycle and integration configuration
statement: ACCSystem keeps a canonical registry of participating institutions with stable platform identifiers, an explicit activation lifecycle and managed integration configuration so later-phase capabilities can be gated on institution status.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-INSTITUTION-LIFECYCLE.md
open_decisions: ADR-017-GATE, ADR-022-GATE, IC-002, ADR-015-GATE, RP-16, ADR-011-GATE

title: Unique stable institution ID
statement: On registration of a contracted institution the Institution Registry assigns one unique platform_institution_id that is never reassigned.

title: Activation status
statement: An institution has an explicit onboarding/activation status and is Active only after an authorized activation step.

title: Institution lookup for platform services
statement: The registry provides institution status and integration configuration to authorized platform services, and dependent flows do not proceed on an unknown status when the registry is unavailable.

title: Integration configuration and credential issuance
statement: On onboarding, integration configuration (connector references, allowed event types, credential or certificate references) is created for the institution under the authentication method selected by policy.
verification_refs: REVIEW (planned): security review of credential handling

title: Credential rotation without disruption
statement: Integration credentials or certificates can be rotated and revoked without interrupting service for the institution.

title: Institution deactivation
statement: Deactivating an institution removes its membership-based access and blocks capability-gated operations while retaining its records.

title: Credential rotation transition
statement: Integration credentials or certificates can be rotated under the approved transition policy: both the old and new credentials are accepted during the transition, then only the new credential is accepted; no duration or uninterrupted-service policy is asserted.

title: Revoked credential rejection
statement: After an integration credential or certificate is revoked, authentication using that credential is rejected.

title: Platform authentication, sessions and identity linking
statement: ACCSystem authenticates platform users and service principals, issues short-lived revocable credentials and fails closed, so every later-phase operation runs in an identified, auditable session.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-IDENTITY-AND-TRUST.md
evidence_refs: CNT-ACC-IDENTITY; CMP-IDN-AUTH; CMP-IDN-SESSION; idea-derived security view §2; CON-005

title: Authenticate platform users
statement: Identity & Access verifies user credentials and issues access and refresh tokens carrying role and institution-membership claims.

title: Credential verification
statement: Identity & Access accepts matching user credentials and rejects non-matching credentials.

title: Issue tokens with claims
statement: After successful credential verification, Identity & Access issues access and refresh tokens carrying role and institution-membership claims.

title: MFA for privileged accounts
statement: Authentication of platform administrators and support staff requires a second factor.

title: Short-lived tokens and revocation
statement: Access tokens are short-lived, refresh tokens rotate on use, and a revoked session or token is rejected on later validation.

title: Brute-force limiting
statement: Repeated failed authentication attempts are rate-limited at the gateway, subject to a lockout policy and logged as security signals.

title: Fail-closed identity
statement: When credential, session or revocation stores are unavailable, authenticated requests are rejected while public routes stay available per route policy.

title: Link institution employee to platform membership
statement: An institution employee may be linked to a platform membership for marketplace access without transferring ACCore-local roles or credentials.

title: Tenant context and cross-institution isolation
statement: Every request and query is bound to an authenticated institution context so one institution cannot read, write or infer another institution's data.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-TENANT-ISOLATION.md

title: Tenant derived from credential
statement: The institution context of a request is derived from the validated token, never from a client-supplied value alone.

title: Cross-tenant denial
statement: A valid credential of institution A cannot read, write or infer institution B data through any ACCSystem API, event or query path.
verification_refs: TEST (planned): automated isolation suite and penetration test (acceptance-test-plan.md item 11)

title: Membership claims
statement: Tokens of institutional users embed their active institution memberships; a user without active membership receives no institutional scope.

title: Audited platform-wide access
statement: Platform administrator access that spans institutions is permitted only under the platform role and always emits an audit event.

title: Platform user, role and administration control
statement: Platform user lifecycle and privileged roles are administered through ACManagement acting as a service client of the platform administration and identity services, with least privilege, approval where required and separate admin identities.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-ADMIN-ACCESS-CONTROL.md

title: Account lifecycle administration
statement: An authorized administrator can activate, suspend and reactivate platform accounts and manage institution memberships, and the change takes effect on subsequent authentication.

title: Role grant with approval
statement: A platform role grant or revocation takes effect only after the approval required by policy; until then it remains pending and visible.

title: RBAC/ABAC authorization
statement: Authorization applies role permissions with contextual conditions (institution, branch, operation scope), and each service enforces its own authorization from resolved role data.

title: ACManagement acts only as service client
statement: ACManagement performs administration only through published platform service APIs and never reads or writes the Identity & Access store directly.

title: Separate admin identities
statement: Platform administrator accounts are distinct from institution ERP accounts.

title: Institution-admin console scope
statement: Institution administrators use the protected console only within institution-scoped functions defined by an approved role matrix.

title: Platform account state enforcement
statement: An authorized administrator can activate, suspend, or reactivate platform accounts; subsequent authentication reflects account state, and a suspended account cannot obtain new tokens.

title: Platform account lifecycle event publication
statement: ACCSystem publishes the corresponding PlatformUserSuspended, PlatformUserActivated, or PlatformUserReactivated event when that account state change occurs.
verification_refs: TEST (planned): account lifecycle event publication test

title: Scoped just-in-time support access
statement: Platform support staff reach institution data only through explicit, institution-scoped, purpose-bound, time-limited support sessions that are audited and cannot confer permissions or entitlements.

title: No privilege conferral
statement: A support session cannot grant platform roles or license entitlement.

title: Least-privilege read-only default
statement: Support sessions default to read-only access unless a broader scope is explicitly approved, and masking applies per approved rules.

title: Session events and audit
statement: Grant, expiry and revocation of support access publish events and audit records.

title: Institutional license issuance and lifecycle

title: Issue institutional license
statement: On an authorized request License & Entitlement validates institution eligibility and plan and issues an institutional license in state ISSUED bound to the institution and product.

title: Reject ineligible issuance request
statement: License & Entitlement rejects an institutional license request when institution eligibility or plan validation fails, without creating a license record.

title: Create institutional license in ISSUED
statement: After an authorized institutional license request passes eligibility and plan validation, License & Entitlement creates a license bound to the institution and product in state ISSUED.

title: Signed entitlement
statement: Every issued institutional entitlement is cryptographically signed by the platform.

title: Activation progression
statement: An institutional subscription progresses ISSUED to ACTIVATED to ACTIVE, and transitions outside the permitted graph are rejected.

title: Renew, suspend, revoke, expire
statement: License state changes are applied by authorized actors or scheduled policy with actor, reason, timestamp and affected institution/product recorded; revocation is permanent.

title: Propagation to ACCore
statement: A license state-change event reaches the ACCore license connector, which restricts or restores licensed modules within the approved propagation window.

title: Entitlement is not permission
statement: License entitlement does not grant platform user permissions, and user permissions do not confer entitlement.

title: Audit record for license state changes
statement: When an authorized actor or scheduled policy applies a license state change (including renewal, suspension, revocation, or expiry), the change is recorded with actor, reason, timestamp, and affected institution/product.

title: Revocation is terminal
statement: A revoked license never returns to Active.

title: License event delivery to ACCore
statement: A published license state-change event is delivered to the ACCore license connector under the Outbox/Inbox rules; event mapping and numeric propagation policy remain open.
verification_refs: TEST (planned): license event Outbox/Inbox delivery test

title: Suspension restricts licensed modules
statement: After a LicenseSuspended event, ACCore restricts the licensed module; no numeric propagation window is asserted.

title: Institutional license validation (online and offline)
statement: ACCore can establish whether its institution holds a valid entitlement for a product or module, online or from a locally verified signed credential, without sending ERP data to ACCSystem and failing closed for licensed functions.

open_decisions: UNKN-003, LIC-003, ADR-017-GATE, UNKN-009, ODEC-014, LIC-001, ODEC-008, IC-008, LIC-004, LIC-005

title: Online institutional validation
statement: License & Entitlement evaluates candidate licenses for {institution_id, product_code} in all states and returns lifecycle status and evaluation result without conflating them.

title: Authenticated, scoped, no ERP data
statement: Validation requires an authenticated caller authorized for the institutional scope and neither requests nor exposes ERP data.

title: Offline local verification
statement: ACCore verifies a locally held signed entitlement against the platform public key, checking workflow, institution/product identity and grant bounds, without a network call.

title: Expiry restricts licensed functions
statement: After credential expiry without successful online validation, licensed functions are restricted unless an applicable grace policy is approved, while separately permitted local ERP operation continues.

title: Separate token issuance and refresh
statement: Issuing or refreshing an offline credential is a separate retriable license-owned operation, not a side effect of read-only validation.

title: Signing key custody and rotation
statement: The platform signing key stays within ACCSystem and rotated keys are accepted by validators holding the active key set; tampered credentials are rejected.

title: Tamper-evident audit of sensitive platform operations
statement: Sensitive platform operations produce tamper-evident audit events with actor, action, target, scope, timestamp and outcome.

statement: Each sensitive foundation operation type (authentication, role changes, support sessions, administrative actions, institution changes, license actions, credential changes) generates an audit event.

title: Required audit fields

title: Append-only and tamper-evident
statement: Audit records are append-only and tamper-evident, with no application path that modifies or deletes them.

title: Audit unavailability policy

title: Privacy-minimal payloads
statement: Audit and event payloads minimize personal data and exclude secrets and payment credentials.

title: Restricted audit access
statement: Audit records are readable only by authorized platform admin/support (read-only) and compliance roles.

title: Authentication audit coverage
statement: Each authentication operation generates an audit event.

title: Role-change audit coverage
statement: Each role change generates an audit event.

title: Support-session audit coverage
statement: Each support-session operation generates an audit event.

title: Administrative-action audit coverage
statement: Each administrative action generates an audit event.

title: Institution-change audit coverage
statement: Each institution change generates an audit event.

title: License-action audit coverage
statement: Each license action generates an audit event.

title: Credential-change audit coverage
statement: Each credential change generates an audit event.

title: Gateway trust boundary and public/authenticated separation
statement: All inbound client traffic enters through a single gateway that enforces transport security, token verification, public/authenticated route separation and rate limiting without hosting business logic.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-GATEWAY-BOUNDARY.md

title: TLS only
statement: The gateway accepts only TLS-protected inbound connections.

title: Token verification without business logic
statement: The gateway verifies each authenticated request with Identity & Access and forwards the validated identity, containing no business rules and making no authorization decisions.

title: Public/admin route separation
statement: Public-zone routes expose no administrative API and administrative routes are distinct from public paths.
verification_refs: TEST (planned): route separation and penetration test

title: Rate limiting
statement: Rate limiting applies per client and route class, and per institution for integration traffic, using policy values.

title: ACCSystem–ACCore connector boundary and connectivity options
statement: ACCSystem and each institution's ACCore interoperate only through one logical authenticated connector contract with approved connectivity options, binding every message to an authenticated institution and preserving institutional ownership of ERP data.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-CORE-CONNECTIVITY.md
evidence_refs: ADR-015; ADR-002; CON-001; CON-002; CMP-INT-GATEWAY; CNT-ACR-CONNECTOR
open_decisions: ADR-021-GATE, IC-001, IC-002, ADR-015-GATE, RP-02, ODEC-001, RP-16, ADR-022-GATE

title: Single logical contract
statement: The Integration Gateway is the only entry point for ACCore traffic and the Platform Connector is the only route from ACCore, with no direct database access in either direction.

title: Connectivity modes
statement: Outbound-initiated connectivity is the default for firewalled institutions and protected inbound mode is available only where approved, both using the same logical contract and semantics.

title: Policy-selected authentication
statement: The authentication method per institution (OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials and/or mTLS) is enabled by security/operations policy and verified on every inbound message.

title: Institution identity binding
statement: The institution of an inbound message is derived from the authenticated principal and a mismatching institution identifier is rejected with 403.

title: Schema and signature validation
statement: Inbound events are validated for transport, signature (where applicable) and schema of the declared type, failing with structured machine-readable errors logged as security events.

title: Institution connectivity state
statement: ACCSystem records each institution's connectivity health (such as CONNECTIVITY_UNAVAILABLE) from connector health and last-sync information and exposes it to dependent capabilities, while ACCore local operations continue.

title: Outbox/Inbox and at-least-once delivery
statement: Cross-system commands and events use durable local intent, idempotent receipt and at-least-once delivery so retries and duplicates do not repeat business effects and unknown outcomes stay recoverable.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-MESSAGE-RELIABILITY.md
evidence_refs: CON-003; CON-009; NFR-003; NFR-007; ADR-005; IF-ACC-EVENT-ENVELOPE; resilience-observability.md §1

title: Atomic outbox
statement: A business state change and its outbound event intent commit in the same local transaction.

title: Idempotent inbox
statement: A receiver records receipt before processing and applies each business effect at most once per scoped key; a redelivered completed effect returns the recorded outcome.

title: Retry and dead-letter semantics
statement: Failed deliveries are retried under policy with the same key, and dead-lettering records a delivery condition, not a business rejection or completion.

title: Per-key ordering
statement: Events needing order are applied in order per partition key where configured, and consumers detect out-of-order delivery by version or ordering key.

title: Event immutability
statement: Published events are immutable and corrections are new events.

title: Common event envelope
statement: Every event carries event_id, event_type, event_version, occurred_at, producer, institution_id, aggregate_id, correlation_id, causation_id and idempotency_key.

title: Retry preserves idempotency key
statement: Failed message deliveries are retried under the applicable policy using the same idempotency key; retry thresholds and schedule are not asserted.

title: Dead-letter classification and safe replay
statement: Dead-lettering records a delivery condition, not a business rejection or completion; before replay of a financial or reservation command the source of truth is queried by key.
verification_refs: TEST (planned): dead-letter classification and safe replay test

title: Idempotency keys, correlation and identity mapping
statement: Commands, events and operations carry stable scoped identities, a correlation identifier and institution identity mappings so duplicates, replays and cross-system flows can be recognized and traced.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-IDEMPOTENCY-AND-CORRELATION.md

title: Stable scoped keys
statement: Every retryable command carries a stable idempotency key scoped to its business operation, reused unchanged on retry.

title: Correlation propagation
statement: A correlation_id originating at the client request propagates through every service, message and integration call.

title: Institution identity mapping
statement: The integration layer and connector map platform_institution_id to the ACCore-local institution reference consistently in both directions.

title: Retention covers reconciliation
statement: Idempotency and deduplication records are retained at least as long as retries, reconciliation and audit require.

title: Policy registry and owner-gate mechanism
statement: Unresolved operational, provider, security and governance choices are held as versioned owner-approved policy values with fail-closed defaults so capabilities cannot be activated on unapproved values.
verification_refs: Sub-requirement rows and section 4 of REQ-PH01-POLICY-AND-OWNER-GATES.md

title: Externalized thresholds
statement: Thresholds, durations and policy values are read from a versioned policy store and are never hard-coded.

title: Fail-closed activation
statement: A capability whose required policy value is missing or lacks an owner approval record is not activated.

title: Immutable policy snapshots
statement: Approved policy snapshots are immutable and consumers record the snapshot version they used.

title: Visible owner gates
statement: Each unresolved decision has a named owner function, activation condition and approval record, and stays visible rather than converted to success.

title: Baseline observability, recovery ownership and data boundaries
statement: The foundation exposes baseline health and metrics, names recovery ownership per domain without inventing objectives, and enforces schema ownership and secret handling needed by later phases.

title: Monotonic version

title: Reliable submission

title: Withdrawn listings not shown

title: Atomic ACCore reservation

title: Accepted outcome content

title: Rejected outcome

title: Duplicate request

title: Timeout is UNKNOWN
statement: A timeout, lost response or interruption after possible dispatch records the reservation as UNKNOWN, not rejected.

title: Safe release of eligible holds
statement: After a definitive peer failure and reconciliation, only confirmed ACCEPTED holds not consumed or linked to a confirmed order are released, idempotently.

title: Unknown release reconciled
statement: A release whose outcome is unknown is reconciled before another release is attempted.

title: Escalation to review
statement: An UNKNOWN reservation unresolved beyond the policy window is escalated for review with its evidence retained.

title: Authoritative inventory and stock commitment
statement: Inventory remains authoritative at each seller ACCore, and stock is committed against an accepted reservation only when that seller receives its authorized order confirmation, with failures reconciled rather than rolled back implicitly.

title: Commit on seller confirmation

title: Commit failure is reconciled

title: Buyer purchase does not command seller stock

title: Warehouse reference handling
statement: Institution-owned warehouse or storage references are carried only where an approved contract defines them.

title: Append-only history atomic with outbox

title: Policy and currency snapshot references
statement: Each SellerOrder stores the policy, tax and currency snapshot references that applied, and later policy edits never alter them.

title: Order confirmation guards and handoff

title: No payment before all holds accepted
statement: No payment authorization or capture is requested until every required seller reservation is definitively ACCEPTED.

title: Per-SellerOrder allocation
statement: Each SellerOrder has a payment allocation with seller, amount, currency, tax/delivery basis, policy snapshot, correlation and idempotency key.

title: Capture policy per seller
statement: The policy resolver selects authorize-then-capture or immediate capture per seller/agreement, and incompatible policies in one transaction split into separate attempts or block checkout.

title: Distinct money states
statement: AUTHORIZED means a hold, CAPTURED means collection, and neither alone means seller credit or settlement.

title: Unknown payment outcome
statement: A timeout or lost response records AUTHORIZATION_UNKNOWN or CAPTURE_UNKNOWN and no duplicate financial effect or release occurs.

title: Capture failure after confirmation
statement: A capture failure after confirmation leaves the order confirmed with a visible payment exception handled by retry, reconciliation, void or refund policy.

title: No raw card data
statement: Raw card data (PAN, CVV, expiry) is never stored or transits ACCSystem stores; tokenization or hosted checkout is used.

title: Provider adapter and webhook handling

title: Webhook authentication
statement: The adapter verifies signature and timestamp of each inbound webhook and rejects invalid or replayed ones.

title: Duplicate event handling
statement: A duplicate provider event yields no repeated effect and distinct lifecycle events of one payment are not suppressed.

title: Scoped mapping
statement: Each provider result is applied only through the durable mapping of provider reference, payment attempt, SellerOrder and allocation, never to order_id alone.

title: Provider isolation and breaker
statement: Provider differences are isolated in the adapter, and an open circuit breaker never defines a business outcome.

title: Payment reconciliation
statement: Payment records are reconciled against provider evidence at allocation level so UNKNOWN outcomes are resolved and discrepancies are raised for corrective action.

title: Resolve UNKNOWN
statement: Reconciliation resolves an UNKNOWN payment operation from authoritative provider evidence before any retry, void or release.

title: Allocation-level matching
statement: Provider lines are matched to internal allocations using scoped mapping and compared on gross, fee, commission, net, currency and status.

title: Discrepancy classification
statement: Unmatched, amount, status and currency mismatches are recorded as discrepancy records and alerted without mutating payment state.

title: Settlement evidence ingestion
statement: Provider settlement reports are ingested when a report contract exists and incomplete runs are marked PARTIAL or FAILED.

title: Void and refund operations

title: Void vs refund distinction

title: Scoped idempotent operation
statement: Each void or refund has an immutable operation identity bound to payment, allocation, amount and currency, and conflicting reuse is rejected or reviewed.

title: Refund within eligible amount
statement: Concurrent refunds cannot exceed the eligible remaining captured allocation; amount and eligibility follow approved policy.

title: Refund failure handling
statement: A failed or unknown refund is recorded and escalated without marking the captured attempt failed or repeating the effect.

title: Eligible cancellation requests

title: Per-SellerOrder compensation

title: Independent partial outcomes
statement: Compensation outcomes are tracked per SellerOrder and a partial result is explicit rather than reported as full cancellation.

title: Cancellation notification and handoff
statement: Cancellation events are emitted to affected institutions with only authorized data, and delivery halts or coordinates per delivery mode.

title: Payment ledger and settlement boundary

title: Append-only payment facts

title: Seller credit separate from capture
statement: Capture creates no automatic seller credit; any credit or settlement state follows only an approved policy.

title: Manual or external payment recorded
statement: A payment completed outside the platform is recorded as RecordedOutsidePlatform only by an authorized actor under approved controls and is never presented as platform-captured.

title: Unresolved settlement visible
statement: Settlement and commission domain decisions remain visible open gates and block activation of dependent behavior.

title: Checkout saga persistence, compensation and recovery

title: Durable saga state
statement: Saga state is persisted before each external command so a restart resumes without repeating possible effects.

title: Compensation only for confirmed effects
statement: Compensation (release, void, refund) is issued only for effects confirmed or reconciled, and never for unknown or ineligible ones.

title: Confirmation write failure
statement: If the confirmation transaction fails after successful payment steps, no partial order exists and the saga retries or escalates with possible effects preserved.

title: Review state not inferred
statement: Operational reconciliation timeouts move work to review states and never infer success, failure or release.

statement: Each external shipment has a stable identity within order scope and duplicate events cause no duplicate effect.

title: Pending delivery visibility
